title: Sharps and concealed hazards
audience: Intake coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may triage, refer, document or support work at a scene where police, coronial or other official authority may apply. This lesson does not grant authority to enter, control or work on any scene, or to handle evidence.
learningOutcomes: Describe the no-touch boundary and withdrawal steps for a suspected sharp.
Refuse hand searches of bags, upholstery and blind spaces.
Name the sharps escalation chain for a fictional scene.

instruction.heading: Sharps and concealed hazards
instruction.body: Needles, scalpels, broken glass and concealed metal fragments can be present even where a room appears clear. A worker who sees a point of metal through a bag during a visual survey does not press, open or reach into the bag. Search and removal are carried out by trained people under the site procedure, never by hand exploration of upholstery, waste bags or blind spaces. Check the condition of any sharps container and whether disposal has been authorised before anything is moved. Isolate the item, mark the no-touch boundary, withdraw people nearby and refer the matter to authorised staff. The NHMRC guidelines advise that sharps are not passed hand to hand, are never recapped, bent or broken, and are disposed of immediately at the point of use in an approved container.

procedure: Stop, and do not press, open or reach into any bag, upholstery or blind space.
Mark the no-touch boundary and move people back.
Check the sharps container's condition and whether disposal is authorised.
Notify the authorised supervisor and record the location, time and people notified.
Arrange search and removal only by trained personnel under the site procedure.
Do not resume in the area until the supervisor has released it.

workedExamples.situation: A worker sees a point of metal through a rubbish bag during a survey.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the worker do with the bag?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not press, open or reach into the bag. Mark the no-touch boundary, withdraw nearby people and refer to trained, authorised staff under the site procedure.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner proposes to check a sofa by hand for needles before it is removed.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Hand exploration of upholstery is not permitted. Trained staff decide on the search method.

equipmentAndPpe: PPE for sharps work as set by the assessment and the plan.
Approved sharps container with a condition and fill-line check.
Training-only inert mock scene with no real sharp.

commonErrors.error: Reaching into a bag or sofa to check for sharps.
commonErrors.prevention: Use no hand search. Refer to trained staff.

commonErrors.error: Moving an item to speed up the work.
commonErrors.prevention: Isolate the item and leave it in place.
Check the container's condition and fill level before use.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Sharps search and removal are restricted to trained and, where required, licensed people. Completing this lesson gives no authority to remove sharps.
The NHMRC guidelines advise that sharps are not passed hand to hand and are never recapped, bent or broken.
Where police or coronial process may control the scene, objects are left undisturbed unless that authority directs otherwise.

qualityStandard: Every suspected sharp is isolated, reported and left undisturbed by the work team.
Sharps containers are checked before use.
documentationEvidence: Sharps report with location, time, people notified and boundary marked.
summary: Concealed sharps are not searched for by hand.
Only trained personnel search and remove sharps.

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker sees a point of metal through a rubbish bag. What is correct?
options: Open the bag to identify it.
Press the bag flat so it is easier to move.
Mark the no-touch boundary, withdraw people and notify the authorised staff.

knowledgeChecks.question: Who searches and removes concealed sharps?
options: Trained personnel under the site procedure.

officialReferences.title: Duties of a person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. The PCBU must protect workers and others so far as reasonably practicable; hazards are eliminated where possible and otherwise minimised; for certain hazards a hierarchy of control applies (the page does not list its levels); duties cannot be contracted out. The page does not cover trauma cleaning, waste or PPE rules. Publisher: Safe Work Australia. The state or territory regulator confirms the adopted law.

officialReferences.title: Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03, first 100,000 of 133,773 characters only. Read: section 2.2 (standard precautions apply to all people), section 3.1.2 recommendations 7 and 8 (sharps handled minimally, never recapped, bent or broken, disposed of at point of use in an approved container not filled past its maximum fill line), section 3.1.3 recommendation 12 (spill response with gloves and protective equipment, containment, absorbent removal, detergent cleaning). Healthcare-setting guidance, applied here by analogy. Publisher: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC).

officialReferences.title: Managing spills of blood and body fluids and substances
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. Standard precautions and PPE for all spill cleaning; clear up the spill before cleaning the area and do not add liquid to a spill; avoid aerosols; leak-proof bags and containers for waste; sodium hypochlorite generally unnecessary for spill management. Victorian guidance only.

officialReferences.title: Forensic cleaning services guidelines
officialReferences.pageDate: Reviewed on 17/11/2025 (no published or updated date shown)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. Victorian scheme for forensic (trauma) cleaning after a work-related death: providers must be registered with WorkSafe, hold a recognised forensic or trauma cleaning certification and hold the required insurance; pre-approval is not required because cleaning must start as soon as possible. Certifications named on the page include the IICRC Trauma and Crime Scene Technician Certification. Not covered: cleaning by an unapproved family member, uncertified providers, deceased estate clean-up including personal belongings, clutter removal, structural repair and non-cleaning costs. The page does not describe PPE, waste handling or a licence for this work, and does not confirm any authority to enter or clean a scene. Victorian guidance only.

officialReferences.title: Cleaning and waste disposal procedures for infection control
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. Three waste groups (general, clinical, pharmaceutical); clinical waste in biohazard bags shown as yellow; sharps into containers that meet the Australian and New Zealand standards named on the page; clinical and pharmaceutical waste collected by waste companies licensed by the EPA and taken to EPA-licensed facilities. Victorian guidance only.

officialReferences.title: Managing exposures to blood and body fluids or substances
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. First response: remove contaminated clothing, wash with soap and water, flush mucous membranes, rinse eyes gently, report immediately; remove from duty and carry out a risk assessment; medical evaluation with post-exposure prophylaxis where appropriate; document date, time, type and circumstances. Victorian guidance only. The page shows its last update as 2015.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a scene, to take control of a scene, to disturb or remove anything that may be evidence, or to carry out regulated remediation, transport or disposal. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate, forensic clearance or any other authority. Police, coronial and other official authority controls many scenes, and their release must be obtained in writing before any work starts, whether or not the property owner or manager agrees. Insurer, property-owner and employer authority is also needed where it applies. Some of the work described here is restricted to licensed, authorised or specially trained people. Where you cannot identify who holds the authority, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever the scene release is unclear, the applicable jurisdiction or the worker's authorisation is unknown, a potentially relevant object has been found, a sharp is present or suspected, a worker may have been exposed, the PPE has not been approved, a waste route is unauthorised, equipment has an unknown exposure history, or a party asks for a clearance or safety claim the work cannot support. Do not handle evidence or regulated material beyond your remit. A stop-work decision is a correct decision and is recorded as one.
